answer: Each identity must file a sonnet price sheet for its timber and post a 60-credit bond. A lot backs one identity: the wharf ledger records its serial on delivery and rejects a second claim on it. An auditor may demand one lot at the posted price; a missed delivery or price mismatch burns the bond. The wharf fee rises by funding source: first 15 credits, kth 15+9(k-1), 1000th 9006; 1000 fakes pay 4510500 in fees plus 60000 in bonds. A rented-timber ring fails because the rented lot is consumed at the wharf on first use. An honest trader pays 15 once and recovers the bond after one delivery.
